post_topic: Why Cloud Decoded is LLM-agnostic — and why that was the only defensible architecture decision
scene_description: A layered architectural diagram shows the Cloud Decoded orchestration stack: at the top, workflow logic blocks labeled 'state machine,' 'HITL checkpoints,' and 'audit trail' sit above a clearly marked abstraction interface layer. Below that interface, three interchangeable model icons — GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and a self-hosted Mistral instance — are shown as swappable components connected by a single config-change arrow. The tension is between the locked, brittle 'ChatGPT wrapper' architecture (shown as a crumbling stack off to one side) and the modular, model-agnostic design where the governance layer never moves regardless of which model is plugged in.
